narration: For thirteen years, every Grand Theft Auto Five player has shared the exact same muscle memory.
title: STEALING A CAR IN GTA 6
subtitle: IS NOW A DEATH SENTENCE

narration: You walk out onto a sunny sidewalk, spot a parked supercar, and press a single button.
Your character smashes the window, connects two wires in three seconds, and speeds off into traffic.
If the cops spot you, you just watch their little cones of vision on your minimap.
title: minimap
subtitle: gta5

narration: You duck into a dark alley for forty seconds, the stars vanish, and the car is yours.
Try that exact same move on Thursday night in Grand Theft Auto Six, and you're dead.
title: THURSDAY NIGHT
subtitle: GTA VI  ·  NOV 19

narration: According to three-hour developer showcases inside Rockstar North, Rockstar completely rebuilt how crime works in Leonida.
Stealing the wrong car in Vice City now triggers a six-layer trap designed to hunt you down.
title: THE SIX-LAYER TRAP

narration: Even if you lose the cruisers, ditch the car, and run home, the cops still remember you.
And the deadliest part of this new system isn't even the police helicopters overhead.
It's a silent digital bomb ticking inside your stolen dashboard that only triggers when you hit the brakes.
Before we look at how that hidden tracker works, look at what happens before you even sit down.
title: THE STEAL
subtitle: Chapter 1

narration: In old GTA games, pulling a driver out of their seat was a guaranteed, automatic animation.
In GTA 6, yanking open an occupied car door starts an unpredictable physical brawl on the street.
Drivers actively resist, and passengers can grab Jason or Lucia and throw them straight back onto the pavement.
While you're wrestling in the middle of an intersection, civilians on the sidewalk aren't just screaming anymore.
Witnesses pull out their smartphones, record your face and clothing, and send a live description to dispatch.
So you might think it's safer to steal an empty car parked down a quiet side street.
Except Rockstar divided every vehicle in Leonida into strict security tiers.

subtitle: focus=both

narration: If you smash the window of a parked car, the alarm blares across the entire block immediately.
To get inside quietly, you have to use physical burglary tools and beat an analog-stick lockpicking minigame.
An old rusty sedan outside the Starlet Motel in Port Gellhorn opens easily with a simple slim jim.
Once you're inside an older model like that, you can hotwire the ignition column by hand.
title: tiers
subtitle: focus=1

narration: But try taking a slim jim to a high-end sports car in downtown Vice City, and nothing happens.
Luxury cars are protected by digital immobilizers that completely block manual hotwiring.
title: tiers
subtitle: focus=3

narration: You can't even start the engine unless you've unlocked a high-tech electronic key cloner from an underground fence.
And even if you have that key cloner, hopping into a random street car creates an immediate combat problem.
title: THE ARSENAL
subtitle: Chapter 2

narration: In GTA 5, your character was a walking military warehouse carrying nine rifles and an RPG in their pants.
Rockstar killed the magic pocket inventory in GTA 6 and brought over the realism of Red Dead Redemption 2.
title: NO MORE MAGIC POCKETS

narration: On foot, Jason and Lucia can only conceal two handguns underneath their jackets.
title: carry

narration: You can carry long guns, like an assault rifle or a shotgun, but they stay strapped visibly to your body.
Walk down a crowded Vice Beach sidewalk holding a rifle, and terrified NPCs will scatter and call the police.
Your real arsenal lives inside the trunk compartment of your registered Personal Vehicle.
And that vehicle size determines how much stolen loot you can actually haul away from a robbery.
A motorcycle holds almost zero duffel bags, a coupe holds a little, and a heavy van holds a fortune.
title: capacity

narration: Think about what that means the second you abandon your personal ride to carjack a flashy convertible.
You just left all your heavy body armor, customized rifles, and duffel bag capacity sitting six blocks away.
If you get cornered by SWAT teams and die with only a pistol, the punishment hits your wallet hard.
GTA 6 separates your money into protected bank funds on the BuckMe app and physical cash in your pocket.
title: cash

narration: Until you physically visit an ATM to deposit your dirty bills, dying on the street wipes out your pocket cash.
Yet losing your guns and cash is nothing compared to what happens when the new police radar locks onto you.
title: THE RADAR
subtitle: Chapter 3

narration: When sirens start wailing in GTA 6, your eyes will automatically dart to the bottom-left minimap.
And for the first five seconds, you're going to panic because the minimap is completely empty.

subtitle: gta6

narration: Rockstar removed individual police blips and vision cones from the radar.
title: NO BLIPS. NO CONES.
subtitle: THE RADAR IS EMPTY

narration: You can't stare at a tiny corner map to cheese your way around patrol cars anymore.
Instead, the outer edge of your screen flashes red and blue from the direction cruisers are approaching.

subtitle: gta6

Even the classic wanted stars at the top of the screen now speak a completely new tactical language.

narration: But look directly underneath those stars, and you'll spot Rockstar's smartest new mechanic: the Heat bar.

narration: The Heat bar displays five distinct icons showing every piece of evidence the police currently have on you.

subtitle: lit=face,outfit,weapon,vehicle,partner

narration: It tracks whether witnesses saw your face, your outfit, your weapon, your getaway car, and your partner.
Even after you escape a chase and the wanted stars disappear, those Heat icons stay active in that neighborhood.
Walk past a beat cop twenty minutes later wearing the same bloody shirt, and the chase restarts instantly.
And if you stole a luxury car without scanning it first, you won't even make it out of the district.
title: THE TRACKER
subtitle: Chapter 4

narration: Here is the secret mechanic that turns a routine supercar theft into a total death trap.
title: THE DEATH TRAP

narration: On Jason and Lucia's in-game smartphone sits a black-market scanning tool called the Waink app.
Before you ever touch a parked vehicle, pointing the Waink app at it reveals its entire security profile.
title: waink

narration: It shows the lock tier, the resale value at a chop shop, the registration fee, and the GPS tracker class.
title: waink

narration: Most players on launch night are going to ignore that app, hijack the fastest car in Vice City, and floor it.
At first, as you're tearing down the highway at a hundred and forty miles an hour, everything feels fine.
There are no sirens behind you, no flashing stars, and no warnings on the dashboard.
That's because high-tier vehicle trackers in GTA 6 are engineered to stay completely silent at high speeds.
The system waits until you think you're safe.
The moment you slow down for dense city traffic, a red light, or a toll booth on the Leonida Keys bridges, the trap springs.
title: THE SILENT TRACKER

narration: A rapid electronic beep starts echoing inside the cabin.
If you don't immediately accelerate back to high speed, that tracker broadcasts your exact GPS coordinates to every squad car in the county.
Unless you've built enough reputation with a high-level vehicle fence who can strip advanced trackers, you can't turn it off.
Even worse, if you try carjacking a police cruiser to escape, every single cop car has a permanent hardware tracker wired in.
Within seconds, you're staring at a full six-star manhunt that covers the entire state of Leonida.
title: SIX STARS
subtitle: STATEWIDE MANHUNT

narration: Surviving a high-heat pursuit in GTA 6 takes way more than just holding down the gas pedal.
title: THE GETAWAY
subtitle: Chapter 5

narration: Rockstar rebuilt driving physics from scratch, blending the heavy suspension weight of GTA 4 with high-speed control.
Roads outside Vice City are narrower, traffic is packed tighter, and supercars spin out helplessly if you take them off-road into the Grassrivers mud.
During a chase, Leonida officers don't just pit-maneuver your bumper, they aim directly for your tires.
Losing a single tire at high speed violently pulls your steering and can flip your vehicle across the highway.
And if you get ejected in a high-speed wreck, your character stays dazed and stumbling for several seconds.
To fight back without triggering the Psychopath rating on your Criminal Profile, you have to use Focus Mode.
title: CRIMINAL PROFILE
subtitle: PSYCHOPATH  ·  PROFESSIONAL

narration: Activating Focus slows down time, highlights hidden officers through walls, and marks vehicle weak points like tires, engine blocks, and fuel tanks.
title: focus

narration: Shooting out a cruiser's tires instead of killing the officers keeps your profile at the clean Professional tier.
Then, to wipe the Heat bar clean, you have to execute a multi-step getaway protocol.
title: THE GETAWAY PROTOCOL
subtitle: STEP 1=Torch the getaway car; STEP 2=Swap outfits from the trunk; STEP 3=Split up, minus one star

narration: In Rockstar's official showcase, Lucia drives the crew's getaway car into an alley, pours gasoline, and torches it.
The moment they pile into a clean van, the vehicle icon vanishes from the police Heat display.

narration: Finally, if dispatch reported a man and a woman robbing the target together, Jason and Lucia have to physically split up.
Going separate ways invalidates the police description of a criminal couple and drops a wanted star immediately.

narration: In GTA 5, stealing a car was a mindless button press you forgot about five seconds later.
In GTA 6, every stolen car is a high-stakes heist of its own, and only smart criminals will survive Leonida.
